title: Count a group of rows
summary: GROUP BY combines matching categories for a summary.
introduction: GROUP BY combines matching categories for a summary. Your task: Add another story row and predict the total.
learningObjectives: Add another story row and predict the total.
Explain the example for count a group of rows

blocks.text: GROUP BY combines matching categories for a summary. COUNT counts the rows in each category.
Use the SQL Run button for examples marked runnable. They use this site's in-browser SQLite database and sample-only table names. A Python example needs Python on your own computer instead.

blocks.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (VALUES('story'),('science'),('story'))
SELECT kind,count(*) AS total FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;
blocks.title: Count a group of rows

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`GROUP BY` makes one summary group for each distinct combination of the named grouping values.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Science has one book, and story has two.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A grouped result is different from a list of every original book. Select only useful group facts.
